supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44 UTC, PowerShell ran the documented \FILE-PIN-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1 script under raj.patel's account on WS-ARUIZ-01.
The same logon session is preceded by a network logon for raj.patel from WS-RPATEL-01, consistent with the stated remote-patching practice.
That PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows 11 KB update, then both processes exited shortly afterward.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs for PROXY-PIN-01 were not collected from 13:25 to 14:10 UTC, so proxy-side details for the PowerShell process's network activity are unavailable. Endpoint connection records still show a connection to the proxy during the process.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish that the 13:44 PowerShell invocation was the exact window ana.ruiz reported seeing around 13:40.
The contents of the patch script and the details of the proxy request are not established by the available records.
unrelated_findings: Separate investigation recommended: at 13:23, ana.ruiz launched hidden PowerShell to export recent Security log events to C:\Reports\audit.csv; the process exited shortly afterward. This is earlier than the alerted activity and should not determine this disposition (T094-00030, T094-00031, T094-00041, T094-00042).

That earlier period also includes a DNS lookup for WS-TWEBER-01 and a TLS connection to that workstation; the records do not establish the purpose of that connection (T094-00033, T094-00038, T094-00040).
